deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): K is the ground domain. f(x) is irreducible over K of degree N, and it is normal: every root is a rational function, over K, of a fixed root r. ρ (written ϱ, which looks like 'e' in the script) is a root of an irreducible φ(ξ) of degree μ. After adjoining ρ, f splits as f(x) = f(x,ρ) f_1(x,ρ) ... f_{k-1}(x,ρ). The goal of the section is a reciprocity: f over K(ρ) and φ over K(r) both split into the same number k of factors, of degrees n and ν respectively, with N = nk and μ = kν.

(A) End of the direct proof that all factors of f over K(ρ) have equal degree (left column, top).
- Assume f(x,ρ) has the minimal degree n among the factors and that r is a root of f(x,ρ).
- Let r_1 = θ(r), with θ ∈ K(x), be a root of f_1(x,ρ).
- On the previous page Dedekind formed F(x,ρ) = ∏_{j<n} (x − θ(r^{(j)})), where r^{(j)} runs over the roots of f(x,ρ).
- [Implicit, mine] Its coefficients are symmetric functions of the roots of f(x,ρ), hence lie in K(ρ).
- r_1 is a root of F, and F has degree n. So the minimal polynomial f_1(x,ρ) of r_1 over K(ρ) has degree ≤ n.
- By minimality its degree is ≥ n, so it equals n. Q.E.D.
- Remark: the theorem persists under successive adjunction of roots of several algebraic equations; the final irreducible factors all have the same degree.

(B) Return to the application (left column, middle).
- φ(ξ,s), for a root s of f, denotes the irreducible factor of φ over K(s), obtained from φ(ξ,r) by substituting s for r. Here φ(ξ,r) is the factor of φ over K(r) having ρ as a root.
- Exactly k distinct such factors exist: φ(ξ,r), φ(ξ,r_1), ..., φ(ξ,r_{k-1}).
- φ(ξ,s) depends only on the block f(x,ρ_i) containing s. Choosing one root from each of the k blocks of n roots gives n^k systems, and each system's product is φ(ξ).
- Write φ(ξ,r) = φ(ξ,r') = ... = φ(ξ,r^{(n-1)}) = ∏_{j<ν} (ξ − ρ^{(j)}) =: φ(ξ,r).
- Similarly φ(ξ,r_i) = ... = ∏_j (ξ − ρ_i^{(j)}) =: φ_i(ξ,r). Here φ_i(ξ,r) means φ(ξ,θ_i r), viewed as a function of r.

(C) The dual statement (left column, bottom).
- Since f(r,ρ) = 0, the polynomial f(r,ξ) ∈ K(r)[ξ] is divisible by the minimal polynomial φ(ξ,r) of ρ: f(r,ξ) = ψ(r,ξ) φ(ξ,r).
- [Implicit, mine] This is an identity modulo the irreducible f, so it transfers to every conjugate s: f(s,ξ) = ψ(s,ξ) φ(ξ,s) for all roots s ('allgemein').
- Hence f(s,ρ^{(j)}) = 0 whenever ρ^{(j)} is a root of φ(ξ,s).
- Because φ(ξ,r^{(i)}) = φ(ξ,r) for all i < n, each f(x,ρ^{(j)}) (degree n) vanishes at r, ..., r^{(n-1)}.
- Therefore f(x,ρ) = f(x,ρ') = ... = f(x,ρ^{(ν-1)}) = ∏_{i<n}(x − r^{(i)}), and likewise for each block i = 1, ..., k−1.

(D) Right column: second proof, using the lemma that every root of f is a K-rational function of every other root, 'after adjunction of arbitrary Algebrale'.
- Let f_1, f_2 be irreducible factors of f over the extended field.
- A root α of f_1 equals θ(β) for a root β of f_2. Then α is a root of ∏(x − θ(β_j)), which has degree deg f_2 and coefficients in the extended field. So deg f_1 ≤ deg f_2.
- By symmetry the degrees are equal.
- Corollary: if r, ..., r^{(n-1)} are the roots of f_1 and θr is a root of f_2, then ∏(x − θ r^{(j)}) has degree n, has the root θr, and has coefficients in the field. So it equals the irreducible f_2. The roots of f_2 are therefore θr, θr', ..., θr^{(n-1)}.
- (The next page then uses this to set r_1^{(j)} = θ^{(j)} r_1.)
errors: No mathematical errors found. Implicit but correct steps: (i) the coefficients of F(x,ρ) lie in K(ρ) because they are symmetric in the roots of f(x,ρ); (ii) the identity f(r,ξ) = ψ(r,ξ)φ(ξ,r) transfers from r to every root s because f is irreducible (an identity in K[r] modulo f(r)).
The notation f(x,ρ) presupposes a fixed polynomial representative in ρ so that substituting conjugates ρ^{(j)} makes sense; this is tacit throughout.
The count of n^k 'systems' refers to ordered choices of one root from each block of n roots; correct but loosely stated.
In the corollary of the right column, Dedekind does not argue that the θ r^{(j)} are distinct; this is not needed, because equal degree plus divisibility forces equality of monic polynomials.

results.what: An irreducible normal polynomial, after adjoining roots of arbitrary algebraic equations, splits into irreducible factors all of the same degree. The roots of one factor are obtained by applying a fixed rational function θ to the roots of another.
results.modern_name: For Galois N/K and any extension L, NL/L is Galois and Gal(NL/L) embeds in Gal(N/K); the factors of f over L correspond to orbits of equal size (theorem on natural irrationalities / extension of base field).
results.usually_credited_to: Galois (1830/1846 Mémoire, adjunction propositions); later Jordan (1870) and Hölder for natural irrationalities

results.what: Reciprocity: f over K(ρ) and φ over K(r) split into the same number k of irreducible factors, with N = nk and deg φ = kν. Explicit pairing of the factors: f(x,ρ_i^{(j)}) = ∏(x − r_i^{(l)}) and φ(ξ,r_i^{(l)}) = ∏(ξ − ρ_i^{(j)}).
results.modern_name: Factorization of f over K(ρ) vs. φ over K(r) via the compositum K(r,ρ): degree count [K(r,ρ):K] = Nnu = mu n, linked by the condition f(s,ρ)=0
results.usually_credited_to: implicit in Galois; this 'reciprocity' framing is known from Dedekind's own Göttingen Galois material (1855-58)

results.what: Use of the term 'Algebrale' for adjoined algebraic quantities.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the Galois-theoretic equal-degree splitting under adjunction plus a reciprocity between two adjunctions. Both are known in substance from Galois, and Dedekind's 1850s Galois-theory work is documented (Scharlau, Haubrich). The page is a careful, clean early proof with an explicit factor pairing, but not a new result.

checkable.asserts: x^3-3x+1 is normal: theta(r)=r^2-2 maps a root to another root (illustrates the hypothesis that all roots are rational functions of one).
Over Q(sqrt2) the normal polynomial x^4+1 splits into factors of equal degree (two quadratics x^2 +- sqrt2 x + 1), so n=2, k=2.
Counterexample when normality fails: x^3-2 splits into factors of degrees 1 and 2, so the hypothesis is necessary.
With f(x,rho)=x^2-sqrt2 x+1 (roots z, z^7, z=exp(i pi/4)) and theta(r)=r^3, the product of (x-theta(root)) is the other factor x^2+sqrt2 x+1 (F(x,rho)=f_1(x,rho)).
Reciprocity in the example: phi(xi)=xi^2-2 over Q(zeta8)=Q(sqrt2,i) splits into k=2 linear factors, matching k=2 factors of x^4+1 over Q(sqrt2) (nu=1, deg phi = k*nu).

transcription_corrections: Throughout the left column the transcription's 'e' (in f(x,e), (ξ-e), e', e_1, ..., e_{k-1}^{(ν-1)}) should be ϱ/ρ (rho), consistent with the previous and next pages: f_1(x,ϱ), f(x,ϱ), (ξ-ϱ)(ξ-ϱ')..., f(x,ϱ_1), etc.
First line: probably 'welches die irreductibele Gleichung ist, der r_1 genügt'; 'welches für die' is a misreading.

'Wir kehren jetzt zu der Anwendung' is likely 'Wir kehren jetzt zu der Anwendung des allgemeinen Satzes auf unseren Fall zurück'; the manuscript seems to read 'Wir kehren jetzt' / 'Kehren wir jetzt'; minor.
Right column, end: 'und erfüllt die Wurzel θr' should read 'und enthält die Wurzel θr' (it has θr as a root).
